messages.author: 69f7d832a0cbc260
messages.subject: Founder effects (coef) help
parts:
Hi Karl,

I am trying to determine founder effects in a cohort of diversity outbred mice and can't work out why I'm getting such high QTL effects (image attached). I wondered whether you had come across this before or knew what might be causing it?

The code used to generate the image is also attached. Please let me know if you need any other information.

Kind regards,

Harry




```{r}

fapr <- fst_genoprob(apr, "apr", tmpdir, overwrite = TRUE)

k <- calc_kinship(fapr, type = "loco", cores = 6, quiet = FALSE)

coef <- scan1coef(fapr[ , "2"], DO$pheno[ , 1], k[["2"]])

par(mar=c(4.1, 4.1, 0.6, 0.6))
plot_coefCC(coef, DO$pmap, legend = "bottomleft")

```

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Founder effects (coef) help
parts:
When one or more of the founder alleles is absent, the corresponding coefficient can't be estimated. It should be NA, but it's difficult to ensure that happens.

You can try using the function clean_genoprob() to set small probabilities to 0, and then run scan1coef() again.

But that still may not solve the problem. I'd mostly recommend focusing on particular locations of interest (such as the location of an inferred QTL) and just getting the estimated effects at such specific locations.

karl

messages.subject: Re: Founder effects (coef) help
parts:
Hello Karl and group,

I'd like to re-visit this issue. I also am mapping in a 8-way cross mouse population (HS/Npt) similar to the DO, but with different founder strains. I too am getting the giant peaks similar to what Harry posted.  In addition, I get large (or small) chunks of NA in the effects output file for some of the strains even though there are no missing genotypes for those strains (or any other strain). For example, I am focusing on a peak on chromosome 19 which has 1115 markers.  Of those markers, the number of NA for each strain is as follows:
A   0
B   125
C   408
D   361
E   0
F   0
G   17
H   286

There doesn't seem to be any rhyme or reason to where an NA shows up, but there are some regions in which two strains have identical haplotypes and one strain shows a pattern of NA and the other strain shows the opposite pattern (small example shown below). This is not true throughout the entire chromosome -- mostly it seems fairly random.

Any thoughts? 

-Richard

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Founder effects (coef) help
parts:
Sounds like a collinearity problem…if those two strains are identical in the region, you can’t estimate both coefficients so it drops one, and which one to drop is arbitrary.

karl
